newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says closely watching Spain's EMU drive.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says closely watching Spain's EMU drive.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he was closely following Spain's efforts to be among the first group of countries to qualify for the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
"I'm watching with great interest and sympathy the enormous efforts made by the Spanish government," he told reporters after a meeting with Spanish prime minister Jose Maria Aznar.
Reporters had asked whether Kohl believed that Spain would be among the first round of nations to qualify for EMU. He added the two politicians had not discussed the issue in particular detail.
Aznar said: "I have high hopes that Spain will achieve its objective to be in the first wave of monetary union and I'm convinced we will make it."
He added Spain's fiscal policy efforts in the run up to EMU were showing "excellent result".
The participants in Europe's single currency will be chosen in 1998 based on their economic performance this year.

As the deadline for EMU approaches, northern Europeans have shown signs of apparent concern that countries such as Italy or Spain may have invested too much political capital in joining EMU before their economies are geared to long-term stability.
